name: Yerevan
title: Holidays in Yerevan
intro: A pink-stone capital of café terraces, ancient manuscripts and brandy cellars, with snowy Mount Ararat on the skyline. Here's what Yerevan is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Republic Square in Yerevan, with its pink tuff-stone government buildings and clock tower reflected in the pool of fountains

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 3 to 4 hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: The FCDO advises against travel near the border with Azerbaijan, well away from Yerevan. Check the latest advice and entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are the best months, warm and sunny without the dry 30°C-plus heat of July and August. Spring brings blossom and clear views of Ararat. Winters are cold, with snow possible.

things.name: Cascade
things.blurb: A giant stairway of terraces, fountains and modern sculptures with views over the city to Mount Ararat.

things.name: Republic Square
things.blurb: The grand central square of pink stone buildings, with fountains that light up on summer evenings.

things.name: Matenadaran
things.blurb: A museum of ancient Armenian manuscripts, with beautifully illustrated books going back centuries.

things.name: Armenian Genocide Memorial
things.blurb: A moving memorial and museum on Tsitsernakaberd hill.

things.name: Vernissage market
things.blurb: An open-air market of carpets, crafts and Soviet curios, busiest at weekends.

things.name: Garni and Geghard
things.blurb: A Greek-style temple above a gorge and a monastery partly carved into the rock, often visited together.

things.name: Khor Virap
things.blurb: A hilltop monastery with one of the best close-up views of Mount Ararat.

faqs.question: How do you get to Yerevan from the UK?
faqs.answer: Wizz Air started direct flights from London Luton to Yerevan in June 2026. You can also fly with one stop via a European hub.

faqs.question: Is Yerevan worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's friendly, good value and full of history, food and wine, with ancient monasteries an easy day trip away.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Yerevan?
faqs.answer: Two or three days covers the city. Add a day or two for Garni, Geghard, Khor Virap or Lake Sevan.

faqs.question: Do you need a visa for Armenia?
faqs.answer: UK passport holders don't need a visa for short visits. Check the latest rules on GOV.UK before you travel.
